other_transformation_page._note: The Overview keeps transformation, residual own use, losses and transfers separate. Multi-flow summaries group by flow; single-flow summaries fall back to product, matching the Refining overview rule. Transformation detail stays disaggregated and is labelled as inclusive of auxiliary-fuel own use. Residual own-use rows already absorbed into an upstream inclusive Common ESTO boundary are excluded using upstream component and non-expanding-rollup contributor metadata, not a dashboard mapping list.

routing_special_cases.reason: Transfers are routing operations shown as their own section under Other transformation.
LEAP currently reports Other sector and non-energy as one inseparable aggregate; exact standalone code 17 remains owned by Non-energy.

sector_pages.rule_note: Supply and top-level balancing rows, including signed international-transport bunkers. Matches generated labels by any component code, not just the first displayed code.
Electricity and heat output, plus directly related power-sector own-use rows. The specific 09.01/09.02 roots take ownership ahead of the broader Other transformation root 09.
Oil refining rows. The specific 09.07 root takes ownership ahead of the broader Other transformation root 09; transfers use an explicit routing special case.
Transformation, energy own-use, extraction own-use, and losses not owned by a more-specific Power or Refining root. Transfers use an explicit routing special case.
Domestic transport final energy demand rows.

total_demand_page.tfec_status: Temporarily disabled because non-energy use cannot yet be separated from aggregated Other-sector LEAP demand.
total_demand_page._note: supply_total = sum of signed values for codes 01 (Production), 02 (Imports), 03 (Exports), and the common 04-05 International transport (bunkers) comparison row. The combined bunker row is used in overview totals so its retained 04/05 source children are not counted again; the detailed children remain available on the Supply page. Bunkers are supply deductions and are excluded from domestic demand. Stock changes (06) remain outside the projection-comparable total.

supply_page._note: Show international marine bunkers (04) and international aviation bunkers (05) separately on Supply when separate LEAP source branches are available. While the combined International transport placeholder is active, show their 04-05 parent instead so every dataset uses the same non-overlapping comparison boundary. The combined row remains available to the Energy balance overview for its supply total. Stock changes and statistical discrepancy are balancing rows rather than projection series. Source their base-year fuel values from the ESTO and LEAP comparison scope, label the boundary explicitly, and exclude them from ordinary line and area charts. For Statistical discrepancy only, multiply LEAP chart values by -1 to align the displayed sign with ESTO; do not take absolute values and do not change the upstream comparison fact. Missing 9th Outlook values are unavailable, not zero.

emissions_page._note: The Emissions page contains exactly two charts: emissions by fuel and emissions by major sector. Final demand is split into Industry, Transport, Buildings, and Other demand. Transformation inputs and own use are selected from the lowest available signed flow frontier and combined into one Transformation and own use sector: negative rows are fuel consumption and are made positive, while positive outputs and transfers are excluded. Non-energy and mixed Other-sector/non-energy aggregates are excluded from combustion emissions until they can be separated. Sources with no sector detail use their declared aggregate_flow_code TFC row without inventing a sector split. Factors and their mapping axis live in factor_sets_config_path; leave factor_set_key empty to use the active factor set. frontier_coverage_tolerance_pj is the PJ gap above which the page warns that retained detail does not add back to a reported aggregate.

leap_demand_sector_coverage._note: page_leap_branches maps each domestic demand page_key to its LEAP source branches. The dashboard workflow resolves aggregate-only sectors from leap_mappings/config/all_demand_aggregated_components.json. International transport is a signed supply deduction and is routed to Supply, not domestic demand. Non-energy remains hidden until exact standalone rows include the configured primary source; the combined Other sector including non-energy placeholder is routed to Other demand by its explicit routing special case.

scope_specific_pages._note: Optional diagnostic alternate-scope pages. Keep disabled by default until each page has been reviewed for production usefulness; when enabled, pages are generated only when matching rows exist in the input data.

pages.page_note: Diagnostic LEAP vs 9th transport detail. This view can include sparse alternate-scope rows that are not suitable for the default dashboard until reviewed.
Diagnostic LEAP vs 9th datacentre demand detail. This view is hidden by default because current fixtures expose only sparse alternate-scope rows.

secondary_pages._note: No secondary pages are published. International marine and aviation bunkers remain on Supply and in TPES without a duplicate International transport page.

sankey_diagrams._note: Sankey generation is intentionally disabled until balance-routing rules define how signed common ESTO flows connect without double-counting.
